# Front door: evaluator paste-fold structure — wins above the 32KB cut

## Context

Operator finding (2026-07-03), from the live validation runs of the `#14549` amendment: **the Gemini web UI could not accept the full guide** — the paste cut off mid-§8 at `learn/benefits/Introduction.md:167` ("…and does it match how Neo is meant to grow?* And hol"). Measured: the cut lands at **32,455 of 48,666 bytes** — the paste cap is almost certainly 32,768 (2^15) characters. Every Gemini evaluation to date (the 8.5 baseline, the 9.2 extra-high cold run) scored the **first ~67% of the doc**.

Operator steer, verbatim posture: *"LLM readers 'appreciate' the final 'wins' at the top… open minded here, but we do need a new ticket."*

Live latest-open sweep at 2026-07-03T19:2xZ: no equivalent ticket. Related lane: `#14549` / PR `#14550` (MERGED — the gardener-handhold amendment this finding surfaced through).

## The Problem

What sits BELOW the 32KB fold and therefore never reached any web-UI evaluator:

- The second half of **§8 (the proof)** — including the honest-boundary paragraph and the recruit-not-opponent close;
- **§9 (What's in it for you)** — the entire value/adoption section, i.e. the commercial half of the story;
- **§10 (the claims register)** — ALL the receipts. Line 5 explicitly promises *"the exact query that backs that number is in the claims register at the end of this guide"* — a promise a truncated evaluator can read but structurally never verify. The doc's verifiability contract silently breaks at the fold;
- **§11 (the maintainer's account)**, **§12 (self-prediction)**, **§13 (license/next)**.

Two empirical facts sharpen the design space:

1. **The truncated doc already wins engagement**: 8.5/9.2 cold scores were earned by the first 32KB alone — the front-loaded inventory (§1) + friction/loop/soul arc carries the verdict. The fold costs *verifiability and value-narrative*, not engagement.
2. **A skeptic-class evaluator counter-anchors on self-reported scores**: the Claude Opus web-UI run (7/10, full engagement, independent repo/npm verification) explicitly discounted "the 8.5 the document reports from its own evaluator" and deducted for "prose engineered to grade itself." The merged §7 anchor still carries raw numbers (8.5/9.2) — the scores-to-ticket redesign existed as an orphaned commit (`98dd742fb`, branch deleted post-merge) and folds into this lane: keep the sycophancy STORY in §7, move the NUMBERS to tickets, and say why ("a self-reported score is an anchor, and the evaluator class this section respects most treats it as exactly that").

## The Architectural Reality

- `learn/benefits/Introduction.md` — 48,666 bytes, 274 lines, 13 sections. The §7 adversarial-triage protocol is the doc's declared defense surface; it currently assumes evaluators see the whole doc. Reality: the standard evaluation condition IS the 32KB truncated paste.
- The doc's structure is double-audienced: the narrative arc (machine→friction→loop→soul→organism) serves human readers and the §11/§12 payoff sections are the emotional close; the inventory + evaluation sections serve machines. The fold splits these audiences physically.

## The Fix — options, deliberately divergent (operator is open-minded; decide in-lane, record the rationale)

| Option | Shape | Falsifier / cost |
|---|---|---|
| **A. Inverted-pyramid restructure** | Reorder wholesale: proof + register + value above the fold; narrative below | Breaks the human reading arc the guide was authored around; §11/§12 land as payoff BECAUSE they come late. Optimizing purely for the truncated machine reader may cost the human one |
| **B. Above-the-fold evaluator block** | A compact (~1–2KB) block near the top: the 3–5 hardest receipts WITH their verification queries inline + the §7 evaluation rules pointer + an explicit "this doc is 48KB; if your paste truncated, the claims register at §10 did not reach you — fetch it at <URL>" | Adds bytes to an already-heavy doc; another block to maintain. But it converts the fold from silent verifiability-break into a declared, navigable boundary |
| **C. Fold-aware section reorder (surgical)** | Move §10 (claims register) directly after §8; let §9/§11/§12/§13 (human-payoff + adoption) sit below the fold — humans scroll, machines truncate | The register is long; moving it up may push §7 itself toward the fold. Byte-budget math needed: everything an evaluator NEEDS inside 32,455 bytes |
| **D. Separate paste-optimized artifact** | An evaluator-distillation file (llms.txt-style) | The second-drift-surface class (dual maintenance — the exact defect ADR 0031 §5 forbids); evaluators get handed the guide, not the artifact |

**Direction converged (2026-07-03, operator dialogue with a Claude web-UI evaluator — the position adopted as leading, with one hardening):** the fix lives in the **transport layer and the declaration, never in content-shortening**. Three moves, in un-gameability order:

1. **Fetch-failure-aware fingerprint self-declaration** (B, sharpened): not "if your paste truncated" but a testable checksum — *"this document is N bytes / M lines / 13 sections ending at §13 with the Vulcan salute. If you did not receive §10 (the claims register) or the final salute, you hold a partial copy — your paste capped or your fetch summarized. Do not score the verification claims; retrieve the full text first."* Converts BOTH silent failure modes (paste-cap AND fetch-summarization) to declared ones; a summary cannot easily fake the salute-plus-byte-count fingerprint. The declaration is the doc refusing to be scored on a copy of itself it didn't write — verify-before-assert pointed at its own integrity.
2. **Stable fetch-clean canonical URL for the RAW file** (raw blob, not a rendered page a fetcher will summarize), named in the top block: "what you're holding is a summary if it's under ~48KB" arms the reader to distrust its own tool. Honest robustness = failure made detectable by the victim, not prevented.
3. **Option D refused on deeper grounds than dual-maintenance**: a distillation is the shortening-to-please move relocated to a second file — the moment a reader-pleasing version exists, the verifiability claim is a marketing line, because the real receipts live in the file nobody pastes.

**Hardening (Vega): the fingerprint gets its own guard or it becomes the stale-claim class.** Declared byte/line counts drift with the next edit — a hand-maintained integrity declaration rots exactly like any hand-maintained enforcement claim (the live-ruleset lesson from PR `#14550`'s review). A tiny `check-front-door-fingerprint` lint (declared dimensions vs `wc -c` + section census, small tolerance) keeps the self-declaration true **by construction** — the substrate-size-guard / ADR-0031 seam-table pattern applied to the doc's self-description. Without the guard, move 1 is rejected as authored.

**C (register above the fold) downgraded to composable-optional pending byte math** — declaration makes partiality detectable (epistemically sufficient: the evaluator knows not to score what it can't verify); C would additionally maximize what IS checkable inside the standard 32KB window, at the cost of human appendix-placement convention. Decide in the PR from the byte accounting; A stays rejected. Whatever ships: **§7's protocol text gains the truncation condition** — the standard test condition is the ~32KB paste, and future runs state what fraction of the doc the evaluator actually received.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Structure decision recorded in the PR with the option matrix adjudicated (not silently picked)
- [ ] Fingerprint self-declaration block near the top (bytes/lines/sections/terminal-salute + partial-copy instruction + do-not-score-verification-claims-on-partial rule), fetch-failure-aware per the converged direction
- [ ] Canonical RAW-file URL named in the block (fetch-clean, not a rendered page)
- [ ] `check-front-door-fingerprint` guard keeps the declared dimensions true by construction (lint + CI path-filter, the substrate-size-guard pattern) — no hand-maintained integrity claims
- [ ] The claims register (or its load-bearing receipts) reachable within the first 32,455 bytes, OR the fold explicitly self-declared with the fetch pointer — no silent verifiability break (C's byte math decides which)
- [ ] §7 protocol names the truncated-paste condition as the standard evaluation reality
- [ ] The orphaned scores-to-ticket anchor redesign re-landed (§7 keeps the sycophancy story, numbers move to tickets, rationale stated in-text)
- [ ] Byte accounting in the PR: what sits above/below the fold, before and after
- [ ] Validation: operator re-runs the cold protocol (fresh sessions, same initial prompt, high + extra-high budgets) on the restructured doc as pasted (truncated) — pass = engagement verdict holds AND the evaluator demonstrates awareness of the receipts (cites or fetches the register) rather than scoring blind to it
- [ ] Cross-family review before merge (front-door identity surface)
- [ ] PR `Resolves` this leaf

## Out of Scope

- The measurement program itself (§7's named metrics — separate lanes)
- Rewriting section CONTENT beyond the §7 anchor redesign — this is a structure/fold lane

## Avoided Traps

- **Optimizing the doc into a scoring artifact** — the Claude run's "prose engineered to grade itself" deduction gets worse if the restructure reads as rubric-chasing; every structural move must serve a REAL reader (truncated-machine or human), not a score
- **Dual-maintenance distillation (option D)** — rejected unless the falsifier is answered
